correctness.rationale: The necessity sigma*(n)>=3n follows from the class containing n. For <=5 distinct primes, each factor (1+p_i^{-a_i}) is bounded by the corresponding (1+1/q_i) for the first five primes, and the product is exactly 1152/385<3; therefore at least six distinct primes and n>=30030. For 30030, the two displayed disjoint subsets have sum 32256 each and its set of 64 unitary divisors has sum 96768, leaving a third class with the same sum. The exact Python verifier reconstructs membership, disjointness, complements, sums and rational inequality. No unproved finite-to-infinite extension occurs.

evidence: Mahanta–Saikia–Yaqubi, arXiv:2008.11096v1, Theorem 3.7 excludes *odd squarefree* ordinary 3-layered integers up to fifteen primes; our witness has a factor 2 and concerns unitary divisors for all possible exponents.
Jokar 2022 establishes the unrestricted ordinary 3-layered minimum 120, but this has prime powers and not every divisor is unitary.

value.rationale: The least element and minimal prime-support size are natural exact invariants of three-way equal-sum unitary divisor partitions, extending two-way unitary Zumkeller and ordinary k-layered studies. The five-prime normalized unitary sum falls short of 3 by only 3/385, so the obstruction is sharp and arithmetically near-critical; the next primorial unexpectedly attains a full 64-divisor three-way partition. This is a substantive exact boundary with a reproducible partition witness, not an arbitrary fixed slice or a mere recoding of the ordinary minimum.
